## Verdict: REJECT (two Important checklist failures: README.md and AGENTS.md say config loading refuses every other URL scheme, but the validator accepts any scheme that starts with "sqlite")

This PR is not ready to merge: two documents the change edits promise that every scheme other than MySQL (and SQLite until its removal) fails at config load, and `DatabaseConfig._supported_url_scheme` in `src/sqllens/config.py` still loads schemes such as `sqlitefoo://` and `sqlite3://`, so either the check must be tightened to `sqlite` or `sqlite+<driver>` or the two sentences must be softened.
Rule applied: rule 1 — a checklist FAIL at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major

- VC-2: FAIL (important) — AGENTS.md asserts that config loading, through the `DatabaseConfig.url` validator in config.py, refuses every URL scheme other than `mysql://` and `mysql+<driver>://` (mysqlx:// included) and a URL with no `://`, while still accepting SQLite URLs until #383, and that the server version is not checked. [AGENTS.md:18]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  AGENTS.md:18 says config loading 'refuses every other URL scheme, mysqlx:// included, and a URL with no ://' (SQLite still accepted until #383). The validator at src/sqllens/config.py:108-115 (DatabaseConfig._supported_url_scheme) is: if '://' in value: scheme = value.split('://',1)[0].lower(); if scheme == 'mysql' or scheme.startswith(('mysql+', 'sqlite')): return value; else raise ValueError. Traced inputs: 'MYSQL+PyMySQL://u@h/db' -> scheme lowercased 'mysql+pymysql' -> accepted (consistent). 'mysqlx://u@h/db' -> 'mysqlx' is neither == 'mysql' nor starts with 'mysql+' or 'sqlite' -> refused (matches). '' -> no '://' -> refused (matches). Non-string -> pydantic str type check fails before the after-validator (refused). Counterexamples to the absolute claim: 'sqlitefoo://x' -> scheme 'sqlitefoo' startswith 'sqlite' -> ACCEPTED, though it is not a SQLite URL and is an 'other' scheme the doc says is refused (the check is a bare prefix match, not scheme == 'sqlite' or 'sqlite+<driver>'); likewise 'sqlite2://', 'sqlitex://'. Also 'mysql+://h/db' (empty driver) is accepted. The SQLLENS_DATABASE__URL env var feeds the same field validator via Config (config.py:756-779), so env input hits the same path; ProfilesConfig carries no database URL, so profile overrides do not reach it. 'The server version is not checked' was not contradicted in config.py (no version check there) but the absolute 'every other scheme' wording is broken by the sqlite prefix match. The Field description at config.py:62-69 repeats the same over-claim.

  </details>

- VC-4: FAIL (important) — README asserts that any URL scheme other than MySQL or SQLite, or a URL with no `://`, fails every `sqllens` command that loads the config, validate and serve included. [README.md:61]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  README.md:61 says 'Any other URL scheme, or a URL with no `://`, fails every `sqllens` command that loads the config, `validate` and `serve` included.' The validator that enforces this is src/sqllens/config.py:108-115 (DatabaseConfig._supported_url_scheme). It requires '://' in the value, then lowercases the scheme and accepts it if `scheme == "mysql" or scheme.startswith(("mysql+", "sqlite"))`. The `startswith("sqlite")` check is a bare prefix match, so it also accepts any scheme that merely begins with 'sqlite': `sqlite3://`, `sqlitecloud://`, `sqlitefoo://`. Those are schemes other than MySQL or SQLite. Config.load (config.py:811-851) adds no further scheme check. `validate` (cli.py:258-273) therefore prints 'Config OK' for `database.url = "sqlite3://x"` unless --check-db is passed. The README's 'any other scheme ... fails every command' is therefore false for that class of input. Positive side: for postgresql:// and any other non-mysql/non-sqlite-prefixed scheme, and for a URL with no '://', the validator raises ValueError. Every config-loading command wraps Config.load in `except Exception` and exits non-zero (code 2): serve cli.py:203-207, validate cli.py:258-262, import-memory cli.py:449-453, verify-memory cli.py:566-570, export-memory cli.py:711-715. So the postgres case in verify_hint holds on all five commands. The README wording is still absolute and is contradicted by the sqlite-prefix hole. claude-desktop install does not call Config.load (cli.py:389-402), which is outside the claim's 'loads the config' scope. The item's claim_provenance is source_authored, so this counterexample in authored text counts as FAIL. The fix is either to tighten the validator to scheme == 'sqlite' or scheme.startswith('sqlite+'), or to soften the README.

  </details>

- VC-10: FAIL (suggestion) — configuration.md asserts that any other URL scheme, mysqlx:// included, or a URL with no `://`, fails every sqllens command that loads the config, validate and serve included. [docs/external/configuration.md:47]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  docs/external/configuration.md:47 says any other URL scheme, mysqlx:// included, or a URL with no `://`, fails every sqllens command that loads the config. The three traced inputs behave as the doc says. In src/sqllens/config.py:108-115 (_supported_url_scheme), `mysqlx://u@h/db` has scheme `mysqlx`, which is neither `mysql` nor starts with `mysql+` or `sqlite`, so it raises ValueError(UNSUPPORTED_DATABASE_URL_MESSAGE). `MySQLX://u@h/db` is lowercased first (line 112) and is refused the same way. `host/db` has no `://` and falls through to the raise on line 115. All five Config.load call sites (cli.py:204 serve, 259 validate, 450 import-memory, 567 verify-memory, 712 export-memory) catch Exception and print _format_config_error, which yields the validation message. The claude-desktop-install validate_toml (installers/claude_desktop.py:352) also calls Config.load. The message text matches the doc.

  The claim is absolute, though, and the validator accepts more than the documented schemes. Line 113 uses `scheme.startswith(("mysql+", "sqlite"))`, so any scheme that merely begins with `sqlite` passes config load, for example `sqlitefoo:///x.db` or `sqlitex://...`. These are not the documented `sqlite:///` forms. They also run: agent/factory.py:241 and preflight.py:111 use `startswith("sqlite")` and build a SqliteRunner. So a scheme other than the ones listed loads and serves without error, and the claim that any other scheme fails every config-loading command is false for that input. A user can reach it by writing it in the config TOML. criteria.json criterion 2 itself specifies `starts with sqlite`, so the looseness is intended by the spec, and the fix is likely to the doc wording (say `sqlite`-prefixed schemes are accepted until SQLite removal) or to a tighter check. The reach is a narrow edge, so the severity is a suggestion.

  </details>

- VC-18: FAIL (suggestion) — The MySQL timeout that fires mid-execution is named `max_statement_time`, the statement-timeout primitive the MySQL runner uses. [docs/internal/database-connectors/cleanup-error-handling.md:9]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The MySQL runner issues `SET SESSION MAX_EXECUTION_TIME = %s` (src/sqllens/agent/integrations/mysql/sql_runner.py:128-133; its docstring at :92 also says 'MAX_EXECUTION_TIME firing'). read-only-safety.md:104 documents the same statement. `max_statement_time` is a MariaDB variable and is not what the runner sets. No `max_statement_time` setting exists in the runner. The authored doc line docs/internal/database-connectors/cleanup-error-handling.md:9 ('MySQL `max_statement_time` fires.') and :16 ('max_statement_time exceeded') therefore name the wrong timeout primitive. The doc's own claim that MySQL is the subject makes this a wrong authored statement (the sql_runner.py:173 comment and tests/unit/test_sql_runner_cleanup.py:30,70,88 reuse the same wrong name as a stand-in error message).

- VC-19: FAIL (suggestion) — On a MySQL timeout the LLM would otherwise receive a message of the form "max_statement_time exceeded". [docs/internal/database-connectors/cleanup-error-handling.md:16]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The doc line (docs/internal/database-connectors/cleanup-error-handling.md:16, with the same name at :9) says a MySQL timeout would reach the LLM as "max_statement_time exceeded". The MySQL runner never sets max_statement_time. src/sqllens/agent/integrations/mysql/sql_runner.py:132-135 runs `SET SESSION MAX_EXECUTION_TIME = %s`, and its docstring (line 92) says the error is "MAX_EXECUTION_TIME firing". The repo's connector test (tests/connectors/test_connectors.py:326-330) records that this interruption surfaces as pymysql OperationalError errno 3024 (ER_QUERY_TIMEOUT). On MySQL that error's server-sent text is, as I recall, "Query execution was interrupted, maximum statement execution time exceeded". The pymysql source was not provided, so I could not read that text in the installed library. `max_statement_time` is MariaDB's variable (MySQL used it only in 5.7.4-5.7.7), and MariaDB's own timeout text is "(max_statement_time exceeded)". It is not what this MySQL runner's configured timeout produces. Only the unit-test fake error in tests/unit/test_sql_runner_cleanup.py:30,70 and a comment in sql_runner.py:173 use that wording. The claim's literal quoted message is therefore not what the LLM would receive on a MySQL timeout. This is a wording inaccuracy in authored doc text. The doc's main point (cleanup errors would mask the timeout error) holds, and this item is source_authored, so a FAIL on wrong authored text is allowed.

  </details>

- VC-50: FAIL (suggestion) — `apply_rls` folds no identifiers and refuses no unquoted non-ASCII identifier under any dialect. [docs/internal/database-connectors/row-level-security.md:56]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Claim (docs/internal/database-connectors/row-level-security.md:56): 'apply_rls folds no identifiers and refuses no unquoted non-ASCII identifier under any dialect'. Second half holds: rls.py has no non-ASCII check or refusal (only uses_table_shorthand, which looks at TABLE keyword tokens, readonly.py:79-121; the only ord() check, rls.py:102, is on dynamic metadata values, not identifiers). First half is literally false: apply_rls does not call normalize_identifiers and its output is tree.sql(dialect=..., normalize_functions=False) (rls.py:318), so the emitted SQL keeps written case. But it does fold identifiers for matching, dialect-independently: rules_by_table is keyed by rule.table.lower() (rls.py:236), base tables are matched with table.name.lower() (rls.py:272), CTE/derived references with table.name.lower() (rls.py:290), and the backstop walk uses name.lower()/alias.lower() (rls.py:298-299). Trace: SELECT * FROM Orders with a rule on `orders`, dialect postgres, mysql or None, gets the predicate injected because 'Orders'.lower() == 'orders'. That is case folding of an identifier, using full Unicode str.lower() (it folds non-ASCII too), not ASCII-only like relations.py:94. It also applies under MySQL with lower_case_table_names=0, where the doc's next clause says lowercasing is conditional. The over-match errs toward filtering, so the security effect is safe; the defect is the absolute doc wording. Under the narrower reading (no sqlglot normalize_identifiers, as the test at tests/unit/test_rls_views.py:260 uses 'fold'), the sentence would hold, but as written 'folds no identifiers' is contradicted by rls.py:236/272/290/298.

  </details>

- VC-58: FAIL (suggestion) — The statement_timeout_ms description says MySQL applies it via SET SESSION MAX_EXECUTION_TIME, SQLite via a progress-handler deadline, and 0 disables it on MySQL only. [src/sqllens/config.py:92]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  config.py:91-93 says '0 disables (MySQL only)'. The MySQL runner does disable at 0 (mysql/sql_runner.py:120,127 only issues SET SESSION MAX_EXECUTION_TIME when statement_timeout_ms > 0) and uses that SET (line 133), so the MySQL parts are right. But the SQLite runner also disables at 0: sqlite/sql_runner.py:196 registers the progress-handler deadline only `if self._statement_timeout_ms > 0`, and line 225 only clears it under the same guard; its docstring (line 122) says '0 disables'. factory.py:246/262 passes cfg.database.statement_timeout_ms to both runners. So with statement_timeout_ms=0 SQLite has no deadline, and the '(MySQL only)' qualifier is false. The PR introduced this wording: the base text said '0 disables (Postgres/MySQL only)', and removing Postgres left a 'MySQL only' that wrongly excludes SQLite. The MySQL and SQLite mechanisms described are accurate; only the 'MySQL only' qualifier is wrong. Authored description text, so a counterexample in it settles FAIL.

  </details>

- VC-66: FAIL (suggestion) — The docstring asserts that PostgreSQL, mysqlx and every other non-MySQL URL is refused at load. [tests/unit/test_config_schema.py:132]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The docstring at tests/unit/test_config_schema.py:132 says 'PostgreSQL, mysqlx and every other non-MySQL URL is refused at load.' The validator `_supported_url_scheme` in src/sqllens/config.py:108-115 returns the value unchanged when the scheme is 'mysql' or starts with 'mysql+' or 'sqlite' (line 113). So `sqlite:///:memory:` is accepted: scheme 'sqlite' passes `scheme.startswith(('mysql+','sqlite'))`. The same test file lists `sqlite:///:memory:` and `sqlite+pysqlite:///x.db` in `_ACCEPTED_URLS` (lines 107-108), and test_url_scheme_accepted asserts they are accepted. config.py:67 also says sqlite:// 'is still accepted until its removal'. Input `sqlite:///:memory:` is a non-MySQL URL that is not refused, so the universal 'every other non-MySQL URL' is false. The parametrized cases in the test (postgresql, postgres, mysqlx, mariadb, empty, no-separator) are all refused correctly; only the docstring's universal wording is wrong. It is a docstring inaccuracy with no runtime effect.

  </details>

- VC-98: FAIL (suggestion) — The comment asserts that "#" opens a line comment only in MySQL, so under another dialect `#x\nSHOW 'abc` is not a SHOW. [tests/unit/test_safety.py:941]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The comment at tests/unit/test_safety.py:941 says '"#" opens a line comment only in MySQL; elsewhere this is not a SHOW.' is_introspection_query (src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:254-292) calls first_sql_keyword, which tokenizes with sqlglot.Dialect.get_or_raise(dialect).tokenize(sql) (readonly.py:139-148), so '#' is a comment exactly when that dialect's Tokenizer.COMMENTS contains it. Installed sqlglot (.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/sqlglot/dialects) has COMMENTS with '#' in mysql.py:89, but also clickhouse.py:80 (COMMENTS = ["--", "#", "#!", ...]) and bigquery.py:150 (COMMENTS = ["--", "#", ...]); MySQL-derived dialects (doris, singlestore) inherit it, while starrocks.py:25-26 explicitly removes it. So 'only in MySQL' is false as a statement about sqlglot dialects: under dialect='clickhouse' or 'bigquery' the '#x' line is skipped as a comment, as under mysql. For dialect='sqlite' (the one the test uses) the claim holds: sqlite.py has no '#' comment (base tokens.py:563 COMMENTS = ["--", ("/*","*/")]), so '#' tokenizes as HASH. Caveats: the test's assertion itself (False under sqlite) is correct, and the shipped URL mapping (sqlglot_dialect_for_url, readonly.py:178-189) only yields mysql or sqlite, so within the app's two supported engines the comment is accurate; the input 'SHOW 'abc' also has an unterminated string, so first_sql_keyword returns '' on TokenError for every dialect and the result is False regardless of '#'. The falsity is limited to the absolute word 'only' as applied to other sqlglot dialects accepted by is_introspection_query's public dialect parameter (not a documented-supported engine), hence low severity.

  </details>

</details>

- VC-30: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — MySQL's `TABLE t` shorthand is rejected on every supported sqlglot version, found by the tokenizer (`uses_table_shorthand`) before the root-type check. [docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md:33]

No dependency_sources directory was supplied, sqlglot source is not in either view (inventory.json has no sqlglot tokens.py or dialects/mysql.py entry), and reading the worktree .venv is not permitted. Not run: `pytest tests/unit/test_safety_table_shorthand.py tests/unit/test_safety.py::test_assert_select_only_refuses_table_shorthand` against sqlglot 30.22 and 30.30.
